text: Quiet morning. Tea by the window, rain on the glass, nowhere to be until noon.
After yoga I felt properly settled for the first time this week. My shoulders came down from my ears.
Walked the dog along the beach at dusk. Just waves and sand and his silly ears flapping. Head clear.
Spent the afternoon repotting plants. Hands in the soil. Very peaceful.
The storm passed and everything outside is still and dripping. Same inside me.
Meditation app said 'notice the breath'. For once I actually did. Ten minutes of nothing in the best way.
Fished with Grandpa Jun at the reservoir. We caught nothing and barely spoke. Perfect.
Long bath, candles, an audiobook. Phone in the other room.
The big meeting was moved and suddenly my whole day opened up. Felt the tension just drain out.
I thought the conversation with Esther would be hard but we listened to each other and I left feeling steady.
Library on a weekday afternoon: old men reading newspapers, a radiator ticking, me and my notebook. Bliss.
Sat in the car outside the house for five minutes before going in. Not avoiding anything, just enjoying the quiet.
Steady day. Did my work, ate well, went to bed early. Nothing to report and that's a nice feeling.
Watched the snow fall from the café window for an hour. Everything muffled and soft.
Rowing at 6am, the lake like glass. Moana and I didn't say a word the whole way out.
Knitting while the radio murmured. Lost track of time completely.
After weeks of noise in my head it's finally quiet. I'm not happy exactly. I'm just at ease.
Camping. Fire crackling, stars, Rafael asleep in his chair with his mouth open. I feel very still.
Was expecting to be nervous before the operation but I felt surprisingly calm. The nurse, Bridget, held my hand and talked about her garden.
Ironed shirts and listened to the rain. Simple tasks are soothing.
Sunday at the allotment. Weeding, the robin following me, mug of coffee on the shed step.
Ended the day sitting with Deepa on the balcony, not talking, watching the city lights come on.
Not stressed for once. Work's under control, flat's tidy, nothing urgent.
Swam forty lengths slowly. Counted strokes. Thoughts went smooth like the water.
Evening walk through the woods with Pablo. The light through the pines was gold. We talked softly about nothing.
The kids are asleep, the dishes are done, the house is warm. I'm just sitting here listening to the fridge hum.
Cancelled everything and stayed home reading. Didn't feel guilty about it, which is new.
Prayer at the temple this morning. Incense, bells, the old priest chanting. I left feeling settled for the whole day.
Even-keeled today. Things went wrong at work and I just handled them one at a time.
Lay in the hammock and watched clouds. I'm 38 years old. Highly recommend.
Talked to Dr. Hughes about the panic attacks. Having a plan makes everything feel quieter.
The train was delayed and instead of getting cross I just read my book. Growth?
Painted watercolours on the porch while the cicadas went. Couldn't tell you what time it was.
Night shift was slow. Mopped, restocked, chatted with Ahmed about his allotment. Strangely peaceful at 4am.
I let the phone ring out and finished my tea. It can wait. Everything can wait for ten minutes.
Hot springs with Keiko. Steam, snow on the rocks, my whole body went soft.
I feel balanced lately. Sleep, walks, fewer screens. Noticing it.
Sat on the hill behind the house and watched the sheep for half an hour. Mind as empty as the sky.
After the funeral everyone left and the house went quiet. I made tea and sat with it. Sad, but calm. Ready to rest.
Gentle day. Baked bread, called Auntie Grace, folded laundry in the sun.
Breathing exercise before the exam actually worked. Walked in steady and stayed steady.
Weekend at the cabin with no signal. By day two my brain stopped buzzing.
Watching Hugo sleep on my chest. His tiny breaths. Everything else fades.
Rain cancelled the match so I spent the afternoon doing a jigsaw. Very relaxing actually.
I was furious this morning but by lunch, after a walk, I felt calm and could see Jorge's side of it.
Silent retreat day three. The urge to talk is gone. Just footsteps and birds.
Slow coffee with Martina on her stoop, watching the street wake up.
Doctor's appointment went fine. I didn't spiral beforehand like usual. Just went, sat, listened.
Tidied the desk, lit a candle, wrote three pages by hand. The world is far away tonight.
Flat sea, flat sky, me on the paddleboard in the middle. I could've stayed out there forever.
Watched the tide come in at the estuary with Niamh. She brought a flask. We said maybe ten words.
Unbothered today. Usually the group chat drama gets to me. Didn't even open it.
Bedtime routine with the twins went smoothly for once. Stories, songs, lights out. I lay on the floor between their beds until they were asleep.
A quiet, settled feeling all day. The decision's made and I'm at peace with it.
Lantern festival by the river. Thousands of little lights drifting. Everyone hushed.
Long drive home on empty roads at night, old radio station, window cracked. Very peaceful.
I'm surprisingly relaxed about the move. Boxes everywhere and I'm just taking it one box at a time.
Played chess with Omari at the park. Slow game. Pigeons everywhere. My mind finally slowed down to match.
Mild, settled day. No highs, no lows.
Wrote a letter to Mum by hand, sealed it, walked it to the post box at sunset. Felt grounded.
Soft rain, the cat curled on my feet, a big pot of soup on the stove. Couldn't ask for more.
Breathed through the urge to reply angrily to Graham's email. Waited an hour. Wrote a polite one. Felt calm and in control.
The waiting is over, the scan was clear, and now I just feel this deep exhale.
Picked blackberries along the lane with Ellie. Purple fingers, wasps, sunshine. Unhurried.
Stillness. Morning light on the floorboards. Didn't reach for my phone.
Today was easy. Kind people, simple tasks, home by six.
Floated in the sea and let the waves rock me. For a while I couldn't remember what I'd been worrying about.
Took the slow train instead of the fast one. Watched the fields go by. Arrived late and relaxed.
After the argument we both took a breather. Now we're sitting together on the sofa, quiet, okay again.
Cleared my inbox to zero, then shut the laptop and sat in the garden. Mind tidy as the inbox.
